thread.title_full: Connecticut Republicans meet to say 'hands off homeschoolers' - NewsBreak

author: Preston Stober
title: Connecticut Republicans meet to say 'hands off homeschoolers' - NewsBreak
text:
By Preston Stober ,
1 hours ago EAST HADDAM, Conn. (WTNH) — After two incidents of suspected abuse in one year sparked conversations about homeschooling reform in Connecticut, Republican state representatives and community members gathered for a meeting in East Haddam with one simple message — keep your hands off homeschoolers .
Republican representatives met with homeschooling families at the East Haddam Grange Hall to update them on homeschool regulations, answer questions and hear concerns about potential policy changes.
“I don’t think it should be touched at all,” said one mother at the meeting.
Many calls for homeschool reform have come in after two recent abuse investigations. Back in March, a Waterbury man accused his stepmother of pulling him out of school as a child and imprisoning him for 20 years in their own home.
PREVIOUS: Waterbury woman accused of holding stepson captive appears in court Earlier this month, 11-year-old Jacqueline Torres-Garcia was found dead in New Britain after she was pulled out of school a year ago. Three people, including her mother, have been charged in connection to her death.
PREVIOUS: Connecticut Office of the Child Advocate says investigation following death of 11-year-old girl is ongoing Representatives at Wednesday’s meeting said these incidents are due to oversight by the Connecticut Department of Children and Families and other state organizations.
“These people have already been under the care of DCF,” said Republican State Senator Irene Haines. “Those are the ones that we need to keep watching.”
Homeschooling parents and community members gave their accounts at the meeting, saying they do not need change.
“I don’t quite understand why my children are at risk just by being home with parents,” said Robbin Anderson, a Branford homeschooling parent.
Others at the meeting said that, just because many homeschooling parents say there are no issues with their own children, that doesn’t mean all homeschooled children in Connecticut have the same experience.
“I have had to unfortunately call in suspicions of abuse for the children that I serve, and I have seen DCF fail repeatedly,” said Sarah Schutz, a former homeschool student and current mandated reporter. “I think that is what is happening here.”
News 8 reached out to the office of Democratic State Senator Ceci Maher, who has been outspoken about homeschooling reform, for comment on the meeting.
“I wasn’t made aware of this meeting,” Sen. Maher said. “I am disappointed I could not hear the perspectives spoken there.”
